acceptance: One registry built from the canonical manifest covers the content, resource, content-and-resource and resource-session shapes with a source-less fallback, implements exactly the declared viewers and declares each surface's preparation, isolation, budgets and readiness; documents route deterministically to their viewer, source and capability (whiteboards, Context Map, Markdown, JSON, CSV, HTML, images, PDF, Office, audio, video, code and the placeholder); unknown fields, undeclared viewers, duplicate ids, a wrong fallback and broken semantic combinations (an editable viewer without its veto, a read-only one with one, an inline surface for an isolated viewer) are refused; every format viewer maps through the same manifest (natively there is no lazy module boundary to check).
The diagram render page loads only its bundled script, style and font; its policy allows no other script, no network and only data images, so file, http and https resources are never loaded.
A cancelled or superseded queued drawing is skipped when the queue advances, and an unavailable result is never cached so a retry can draw.

reason: TS draws diagrams in a separate hidden renderer process owned by Electron main: it waits for confirmed process exit before the next job, restarts a new process after a timeout, keeps a slot when exit is unconfirmed, tears an idle host down, bounds requests per IPC sender, validates IPC input and needs an explicit asset root. Natively each window draws in its own hidden WebView with a deduplicated queue, per-slot cancellation, a 15 s timeout and an unavailable cooldown, its assets compiled in (render_service tests).
